title: What keeps the hull afloat?
summary: How requested mass changes the level hull’s immersion in still water—and what this calculation cannot tell us.

sections.title: The question
sections.text: How far does the hull settle into still water as the requested mass increases? The H0 R03 displacement study evaluates freshwater at 998 kg/m³ and seawater at 1,025 kg/m³, with pitch and roll held at zero.

sections.title: What the calculation shows
sections.text: At a requested mass of 40 kg, the calculated level immersion in seawater is approximately 0.0705 m. At 80 kg it is approximately 0.1318 m. These are samples of a level-attitude displacement curve, not equilibrium solutions for a particular rider or component arrangement.

sections.title: Assumptions and limitations
sections.text: The model is a sealed external envelope. Openings, intake and seals are not modelled. The 100 kg request is unachievable in both source series and is omitted from the plotted curves. No uncertainty band is supplied. This is not a physical test, dynamic performance result or safe-payload rating.

sections.title: What comes next
sections.text: Actual loaded equilibrium cases require fuel capacity, fuel density and liquid centre of gravity, plus rider mass, stance and body centre of gravity. Clearance to real openings must also be assessed before operational conclusions are drawn.

changes: Initial website summary of the existing R03 study. No new engineering result.

title: Reading the hull surface
summary: Sections, fairness and feature intent provide a record of the geometry investigation.

sections.title: The question
sections.text: How can the hull surface be examined consistently without replacing the intended shape with an idealised one? The R02 archive includes transverse sections, longitudinal views, fairness analysis and a feature-intent review.

sections.title: The record
sections.text: These records make the surface investigation traceable. The full-hull fairness report identifies itself as a completed geometric review, not an acceptance test. A study revision does not establish that the board has been redesigned or that performance has improved.

sections.title: Keep the reference intact
sections.text: The original engineering files remain the reference. Website images are derived presentation assets. Older study records remain available so later decisions can be related to the evidence that informed them.

sections.title: Next steps
sections.text: Any later geometry change should be linked to the issue it addresses and checked using compatible measurements. Performance improvements need simulation or test evidence with stated conditions.

changes: Initial archive summary. Detailed plots remain in the engineering source files.

title: Before this hull, there was an idea.
summary: Original layout sketches and transparent renders preserve the earlier design direction.

Archived component-layout render. It is not the current H0 R03 assembly.

sections.title: The starting point
sections.text: The project archive contains layout drawings and renders showing an earlier complete-board concept. They capture the relationship between the deck, handles, internal packaging and outer shape.

sections.title: Why preserve it?
sections.text: A development record should retain the alternatives and earlier stages, not replace them every time a new model appears. These assets show a previous design direction. Their exact dates and relationship to physical prototypes are not yet confirmed.

sections.title: From concept to evidence
sections.text: The current website places these archive assets alongside the H0 engineering studies. The historical board renders and current hull are different records; they should not be read as a measured before-and-after performance comparison.

sections.title: Next steps
sections.text: Confirm the archive chronology and connect each design change to its rationale, supporting files and eventual test results. Original dates and captions can be added without removing earlier entries.

title: First, establish the reference.
summary: A consistent coordinate system makes later measurements easier to compare.

sections.title: The question
sections.text: Before comparing hull sections or centre-of-gravity positions, the direction and origin of the measurements need to be explicit. The reference-verification archive documents top, side, bow and stern views.

sections.title: The convention
sections.text: The Wahoo reference uses +X forward, +Y port and +Z up. Engineering stationing and physical geometry are distinct: a stationing datum must not be used to flatten or replace the shaped stern.

sections.title: What this establishes
sections.text: This record supports a consistent description of the hull. It is a reference check, not evidence of hydrodynamic performance or a physical acceptance test.

sections.title: Next steps
sections.text: Keep subsequent source revisions and coordinate conventions attached to each published measurement so comparisons can be checked.
